changes.before: Change the constructor’s minutes argument to 15. What prints?
changes.after: Group related data in a record and read it with generated methods.

before: record Session(String topic, int minutes) declares components and supplies a canonical constructor, accessors named topic() and minutes(), and component-based equals/hashCode/toString behavior.

Record component fields are final and the record class is final. A record is only shallowly immutable: a component referring to a mutable list can still observe list mutation unless you arrange defensive copying.
The String and int components used here do not expose a mutable list. The accessors are methods, not public fields; session.minutes() reads the component.

Expected output or behavior: Read 10
. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Create two records with equal components and compare equals, then change one component in a new instance. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A record is a compact class for carrying data. Its named pieces are components. Java supplies a matching constructor, methods to read the components, and equals, hashCode, and toString methods based on them.

Record fields are final, so they cannot be reassigned later. A record class also cannot have child classes. A referenced object may still change: a record holding a changeable list does not automatically freeze that list.
This record holds a String and an int. The methods topic() and minutes() read those components. Their parentheses show that these are method calls, not direct field access.
The program prints Read 10. The two reading methods return the values stored when this Session was made.
The quiz changes the input used to make the record. final prevents later reassignment; it does not require every new record to start with the same data.

before.question: Change the constructor’s minutes argument to 15. What prints?
choices: Read 15 from the new record’s component
Read 10 because records cannot be constructed with new values
A compilation error because records have no constructors
before.explanation: Final components prevent later reassignment; they do not force every new instance to have identical component values.

after.question: Change the constructor's minutes input to 15. What prints?
choices: Read 15, using the new record's stored value.
Read 10, because every record must have the same values.
A compilation error, because records have no constructors.
after.explanation: This new Session is created with fifteen minutes, so minutes() returns fifteen.
